questions.question: Ustad Bismillah Khan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.questionHtml: Ustad Bismillah Khan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Shehnai

Key Points

  • Ustad Bismillah Khan was a renowned Indian musician known for his virtuosity in playing the Shehnai.
  • He was born on 21 March 1916 in Dumraon, Bihar, India.
  • Ustad Bismillah Khan brought the Shehnai to the concert stage and elevated its status in Indian classical music.
  • He was awarded numerous honors, including the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 2001.
  • His contribution to Indian music has made the Shehnai a well-recognized and respected instrument worldwide.

Additional Information

  • The Shehnai is a traditional Indian wind instrument similar to the oboe, known for its distinct, melodious sound.
  • It is widely used in North Indian weddings and religious ceremonies.
  • Ustad Bismillah Khan's performances have been instrumental in popularizing the Shehnai on a global scale.
  • He performed at the Red Fort in Delhi on the eve of India's Independence in 1947, which remains a significant moment in Indian history.
  • His legacy continues to inspire musicians and music lovers across the world.

questions.question: Who explained the system of classifying musical instruments into Tata, Sushira, Avanaddha and Ghana in his treatise 'Natya Shastra' in the early 2 nd century?
questions.questionHtml: Who explained the system of classifying musical instruments into Tata, Sushira, Avanaddha and Ghana in his treatise 'Natya Shastra' in the early 2<sup>nd</sup> century?
questions.solution: Bharata Muni, in his treatise *Natya Shastra* (2nd century CE), classified musical instruments into Tata (stringed), Sushira (wind), Avanaddha (percussion with a membrane), and Ghana (solid). His work integrates art, drama, dance, and music, forming the foundation of Indian classical music's study and showcasing ancient India's cultural richness.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a stringed instrument?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a stringed instrument?
questions.solution: The Flute is a woodwind instrument, not a stringed instrument, as it produces sound when air is blown across its opening, causing internal vibrations. Stringed instruments, such as the Guitar, Violin, and Mandolin, produce sound through the vibration of strings made from materials like nylon, steel, or gut, which are plucked, strummed, or played with a bow. The Guitar is widely used across genres like rock, jazz, and classical music. The Violin, known for its high pitch, is common in classical music and orchestras. The Mandolin, with its bright sound, is often found in folk and bluegrass music.

Additional Information

questions.question: Select the musical instrument which is NOT played by way of percussion or NOT played by way of striking any object?
questions.questionHtml: Select the musical instrument which is NOT played by way of percussion or NOT played by way of striking any object?
questions.solution: The Shehnai is a wind instrument played by blowing air into it, unlike percussion instruments like Pakhawaj, Drum, and Tabla, which are played by striking. It is prominent in traditional Indian music, particularly during auspicious events and ceremonies, known for its distinct melodious sound. The Shehnai is considered to bring good luck and is vital in North Indian weddings and festivals. Made of wood with a double reed and a flared bell, it has been popularized by musicians like Ustad Bismillah Khan. Mastery of the Shehnai requires significant practice in breath and finger control.

questions.question: Indian musician Jagjit Singh is credited for the revival of ______ genre of music / poetry.
questions.questionHtml: Indian musician Jagjit Singh is credited for the revival of ______ genre of music / poetry.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ghazal.

Key Points

  • Jagjit Singh:-
    • He was born on February 8, 1941, in Lahore, Punjab.
    • He received his bachelor's degree in English literature from Delhi University.
    • Jagjit Singh is credited for the revival of the ghazal genre of music and poetry. (Hence option 3 is correct)
    • Jagjit Singh has been awarded numerous awards for his singing, including the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and National Awards. He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2002.
    • ​Some of his most famous ghazals include:
      • Aaj Phir Tumko Dekha To
      • Tumse Milne Ko Jee Chahta Hai
      • Dil Mein Tu Hai
      • Mere Dil Mein Tum Hi Ho
      • Woh Kaun Si Gali Hai

Additional Information

  • Ghazals:-
    • These are a form of lyric poetry originating in the Arabic-speaking world.
    • They are typically short poems, consisting of five to fifteen rhyming couplets.
    • Each couplet is independent, but the ghazal as a whole has a thematic unity.
    • Ghazals often deal with themes of love, longing, separation, and the pain of loss.
  • Sufism:-
    • It is a mystical tradition within Islam.
    • It emphasizes introspection, spiritual closeness with God, and the purification of the soul.
    • Sufis seek to achieve direct personal experience of God through a variety of practices, including prayer, meditation, and chanting.
  • Jazz:-
    • It is a music genre that originated in the African-American communities of New Orleans, Louisiana, in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, with its roots in blues and ragtime.
    • Jazz is characterized by swing and blue notes, complex chords, call and response vocals, polyrhythms and improvisation. Jazz has roots in European harmony and African rhythmic rituals.

questions.question: Which of the following is the birthplace of Tansen?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the birthplace of Tansen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gwalior.

Key Points

  • Tansen born in Behata or Gwalior was an Indian musician and poet who was an important figure in the North Indian tradition of Hindustani classical music.
  • Born in a Hindu brahmin family, he learnt and perfected his art in the northwest region of modern Madhya Pradesh.
  • Tansen was a composer, musician and vocalist, to whom many compositions have been attributed in northern regions of the Indian subcontinent.
  • He was also an instrumentalist who popularized and improved musical instruments. He is among the most influential personalities in the North Indian tradition of Indian classical music, called Hindustani.

Additional Information

  • ​The navratnas of Akbar's Court are Abul Fazl, Abdul Rahim Khan-I-Khana, Birbal, Mulla Do-Piyaza Faizi, Raja Man Singh, Raja Todar Mal, Fakir Aziao-Din and Tansen.
  • Abul Fazl, Akbar's friend and counsellor, helped him frame the idea of Sulh-i Kul so that he could govern a society composed of many religions, cultures and castes.
  • Khanzada Mirza Khan Abdul Rahim, generally known as simply Rahim and titled Khan-i-Khanan, was a poet who lived in India during the rule of Mughal emperor Akbar, who was his mentor.
  • He was one of the nine main ministers in his court, known as the Navaratnas.
  • Man Singh I, popularly known as Mirza Raja Man Singh was the 29th Kachwaha Rajput Raja of Amer, later known as Jaipur state, in Rajputana.

questions.question: Identify the Indian musician who is associated with wind instrument (played by blowing).
questions.questionHtml: Identify the Indian musician who is associated with wind instrument (played by blowing).
questions.solution: Bismillah Khan was a renowned Indian musician famous for playing the shehnai, a traditional wind instrument. He played a pivotal role in popularizing the shehnai and elevated its status in classical music. Khan performed at significant events, including India's independence ceremony in 1947, and received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honor. He is celebrated for his deep emotional expressions through the shehnai. In contrast, Vishwa Mohan Bhat is known for the mohan veena, Pandit Ravi Shankar for the sitar, and Pandit Deen Dayal was a prominent politician, not a musician.

questions.question: Which of the following musicians belonged to the state of Assam?

questions.question: Which of the following song forms are sung in the rainy season in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following song forms are sung in the rainy season in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution: Kajri is a renowned folk song of Uttar Pradesh sung during the rainy season, primarily in the Bhojpuri language. It reflects themes of longing, love, and the beauty of dark clouds. Radha and Krishna's divine love often features in Kajri songs. Other forms like Chaiti and Rasia belong to different seasons or contexts.

questions.question: Who is the first Indian classical musician to perform at United Nations?
questions.questionHtml: Who is the first Indian classical musician to perform at United Nations?
questions.solution: MS Subbulakshmi was the first Indian classical musician to perform at the United Nations General Assembly in 1966. She was a leading exponent of Carnatic music and the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1998. Subbulakshmi also received the Ramon Magsaysay award in 1974 and other prestigious awards including the Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan, Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, and the Indira Gandhi Award for National Integration. Bhimsen Joshi, Pt. Jasraj, and Ustad Zakir Hussain are other notable Indian musicians but did not achieve this particular milestone.

questions.question: Pandit Jasraj, the doyen of Hindustani classical music, was a proponent of which of the following gharanas?
questions.questionHtml: Pandit Jasraj, the doyen of Hindustani classical music, was a proponent of which of the following gharanas?
questions.solution: Pandit Jasraj was a renowned Indian classical vocalist of the Mewati Gharana. Other significant Gharanas of Indian classical music include Gwalior, Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, and Rampur-Sahaswan, each with its own founder.

questions.question: Which of the following instruments has its strings made of horse-hair?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following instruments has its strings made of horse-hair?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chinkara.

Key Points

  • Strings of Chinkara are made of horsehair.
    • Chinkara is a bowed string instrument.
    • It has three strings, 2 horsehairs, 1 steel.
    • It is a local instrument found in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.

Additional Information

  • Ektara
    • Ektara is a stringed instrument made of bamboo, parchment and steel.
    • It is found in Maharashtra.
  • Ravanhatta
    • It is an ancient bowed string instrument.
    • It is made of a long piece of bamboo that is set into a dried coconut shell.
  • Khamak
    • It is a string instrument similar to Ektara.
    • It is generally used in Bengali boul (folk) songs

questions.question: Who among the following became the first Indian to be invited to perform at the prestigious Lincoln Centre Hall in the United States of America?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following became the first Indian to be invited to perform at the prestigious Lincoln Centre Hall in the United States of America?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bismillah Khan.Key Points

  • Bismillah Khan became the first Indian to be invited to perform at the prestigious Lincoln Centre Hall in the United States of America.
  • He also took part in the World Exposition in Montreal, the Cannes Art Festival, and in the Osaka Trade Fair.
  • So well known did he become internationally that an auditorium in Teheran was named after him — Tahar Mosiquee Ustaad Bismillah Khan.
  • National awards like the Padma Shri, the Padma Bhushan, and the Padma Vibhushan were conferred on him.
  • In 2001, Ustad Bismillah Khan was awarded India’s highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna.
Additional Information
  • M.S. Subbulakshmi was a renowned Carnatic vocalist and the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna.
  • She performed at several prestigious venues around the world including the United Nations General Assembly in 1966.
  • Zakir Hussain and Ravi Shankar are also renowned Indian musicians who have performed at several prestigious venues around the world.
